Subject: Post-call: Autoscale SLO / burst capacity follow-up

Hi Sarah / Michael 

Great to speak earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side based on the discovery: 

Summary of requirements we heard
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 250ms for chat completions, p99 target 600ms for 1k concurrent users
- Throughput: sustained 120 tokens/sec across peak endpoints, with 3x burst for marketing/promotions windows
- Concurrency: up to 1,000 concurrent sessions with average sequence length 120 tokens
- Streaming: client stream-first integration required (server-sent events) with per-token latency sensitivity
- Availability: regional failover between us-west and us-east; warm pool preferred for <30s scale-up

Autoscale / capacity considerations we discussed
- Warm pools: keep N warm nodes to cover typical ramp; estimate warm pool of 10-15 GPUs based on current traffic profile
- Scale-up times: cold-start to full capacity measured at ~90s for model variants with cold weights; warm pool reduces to sub-10s for request-ready state
- Queueing behavior: Redwood can queue up to X requests briefly while scaling and return progress/estimated wait; we recommend graceful degradation with lower-quality model fallback at >45s queue

Attachments: I attached a short tech note that outlines warm pool sizing heuristics and early queueing policies (redwood-autoscale-tech-note.pdf) and a sample SLO latency workbook (slo-latency-summary.xlsx).

Next steps
1) Confirm the p95/p99 targets above are correct for FastPay (Sarah)
2) Share a recent 7-day traffic export (timestamps, request rates, avg tokens) so our SRE can model warm pool sizing (Michael)
3) Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive  propose Tue 12/2 or Wed 12/3

I'll loop in Dev and Dylan for sizing questions; action items below.

Thanks,

Hi all  quick technical notes ahead of tomorrow's deep-dive: 

Failure modes and client behavior (short answer):
- If capacity is immediately available: requests stream normally.
- If we're spinning up warm pools: we can hold requests in a short queue and return a streaming progress/est. wait header. We default to a circuit-breaker at 45s; beyond that we recommend client fall back to a smaller model variant or a degraded response with cached content.
- If capacity is exhausted and queue > threshold: we can return 503 with Retry-After, or route to a lower-cost variant automatically based on policy.

Autoscale knobs:
- Warm pool sizing: we recommend keeping a baseline warm pool sized for 1.2x typical sustained concurrency for critical endpoints.
- Fast warm-up path: container weights preloaded and KV caches warmed reduces token latency from ~600ms to ~80-120ms in our tests.
- Burst policy: we keep a reserved burst buffer (credit-based) that allows 3x for short windows; extended bursts will consume reserved capacity and then trigger queue/fallback.

On the deep-dive we'll bring a short sim that models your 7-day export and shows expected p95/p99 under different warm pool sizes.

Dev
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
